subproblem.title: Exterior derivative commutes with parametric integrals over [0, 1]
subproblem.statement:
Let N, k ∈ ℕ and let h : ℝ × ℝ^N → Λ^k(ℝ^N) be C^∞, i.e. h : ℝ × Euclid N → Covector (Euclid N) k with ContDiff ℝ ⊤ h. Here Λ^k(ℝ^N) is the space of continuous alternating k-forms, which is finite-dimensional and hence a complete normed space. Then for every x ∈ ℝ^N,
 d(y ↦ ∫_0^1 h(t, y) dt)(x) = ∫_0^1 d(y ↦ h(t, y))(x) dt,
where d is the exterior derivative (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv). Both integrals are interval integrals over [0, 1], in Λ^k(ℝ^N) on the left and in Λ^{k+1}(ℝ^N) on the right.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (h : ℝ × Euclid N → Covector (Euclid N) k), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) h → ∀ x : Euclid N, exteriorDerivative (fun y : Euclid N => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, h (t, y)) x = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, exteriorDerivative (fun y : Euclid N => h (t, y)) x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the supplied proof of radial_homotopy. The specific integrand h(t, x) = t^q ι_x β(t x) is replaced by an arbitrary C^∞ family; the argument is unchanged.

Notation.
- Λ^j := Covector (Euclid N) j, the continuous alternating j-linear forms on ℝ^N with the operator norm. It is finite-dimensional, hence complete.
- alt := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin : L(ℝ^N, Λ^k) → Λ^{k+1}. It is a continuous linear map (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Euclid N) ℝ).
- D := fderiv ℝ. For every ω : ℝ^N → Λ^k and every y, dω(y) = exteriorDerivative ω y = extDeriv ω y = alt(Dω(y)). This holds by unfolding the definitions and needs no differentiability hypothesis.
- h_t(y) := h(t, y) for t ∈ ℝ, and F(y) := ∫_0^1 h(t, y) dt.
- inr := ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ ℝ (Euclid N) : ℝ^N →L ℝ × ℝ^N, v ↦ (0, v).

1. Derivative of F. Apply the sibling param_integral (the accepted cmcdt_lpo_slice_param_integral) with this N, V := Λ^k (a complete real normed space) and this h. Its second conclusion at x says that F has Fréchet derivative ∫_0^1 Dh_t(x) dt at x, where Dh_t(x) = fderiv ℝ (y ↦ h(t, y)) x. The Fréchet derivative is unique (HasFDerivAt.fderiv), so DF(x) = ∫_0^1 Dh_t(x) dt, an interval integral in L(ℝ^N, Λ^k).
2. Partial derivative. Fix t. Since h is C^∞, it is differentiable at (t, x). The map y ↦ (t, y) has derivative inr at x (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_right t x). By the chain rule, y ↦ h(t, y) has derivative Dh(t, x) ∘L inr at x. Hence Dh_t(x) = Dh(t, x) ∘L inr.
3. Continuity in t. Since h is C^∞, in particular C^1, Dh : ℝ × ℝ^N → L(ℝ × ℝ^N, Λ^k) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). The map t ↦ (t, x) is continuous, and right composition with the fixed map inr is continuous (Continuous.clm_comp with a constant). By step 2, t ↦ Dh_t(x) = Dh(t, x) ∘L inr is a continuous map ℝ → L(ℝ^N, Λ^k). Hence it is interval integrable on [0, 1] (Continuous.intervalIntegrable).
4. alt commutes with the integral. alt is a continuous linear map between complete spaces, and t ↦ Dh_t(x) is interval integrable. So ∫_0^1 alt(Dh_t(x)) dt = alt(∫_0^1 Dh_t(x) dt) (ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm).
5. Conclusion.
 dF(x) = alt(DF(x))
  = alt(∫_0^1 Dh_t(x) dt)   (step 1)
  = ∫_0^1 alt(Dh_t(x)) dt   (step 4)
  = ∫_0^1 dh_t(x) dt   (definition of d).
 This is the claim. ∎

Implementation note (verified in Lean during decomposition, about 20 lines, standard axioms only; not part of the proof):
- After intro N k h hh x, put hpi := (Submission.cmcdt_lpo_slice_param_integral N (Covector (Euclid N) k) h hh).2 x and hdiff := hh.differentiable (by simp).
- Step 2: ((hdiff (t, x)).hasFDerivAt.comp x (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_right t x)).fderiv.
- Step 3: simp_rw with step 2, then ((hh.continuous_fderiv (by simp)).comp (continuous_id.prodMk continuous_const)).clm_comp continuous_const.
- Unfold the goal with show ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ _ x) = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ (fun y : Euclid N => h (t, y)) x), then rw [hpi.fderiv].
- Covector is an abbrev that carries the ContinuousAlternatingMap instances, so unification with the normed-space instances fails unless the types are given explicitly. Use:
 - Continuous.intervalIntegrable (μ := volume) (E := Euclid N →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid N) k) hcont 0 1;
 - ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm (𝕜 := ℝ) (E := Euclid N →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid N) k) (F := Covector (Euclid N) (k + 1)) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Euclid N) ℝ (n := k)) hint;
 - then finish with simpa using this.symm.
proof_key_steps: By the sibling param_integral with V := Λ^k, F(y) = ∫_0^1 h(t, y) dt has DF(x) = ∫_0^1 D[y ↦ h(t, y)](x) dt.
Chain rule: D[y ↦ h(t, y)](x) = Dh(t, x) ∘L inr. It is continuous in t because h is C^1, hence interval integrable on [0, 1].
alt = alternatizeUncurryFin is a continuous linear map, so it commutes with the interval integral (intervalIntegral_comp_comm).
dF(x) = alt(DF(x)) = alt(∫_0^1 Dh_t(x) dt) = ∫_0^1 alt(Dh_t(x)) dt = ∫_0^1 dh_t(x) dt.

subproblem.title: Pointwise radial Cartan identity for the dilated form t^q ι_y β(t y)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, q ∈ ℕ and let β : ℝ^P → Λ^{q+1}(ℝ^P) be a (q+1)-form (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q+1)). Let t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^P, and assume β is differentiable at t•x. Then
 d(y ↦ t^q • ι_y(β(t•y)))(x) + t^{q+1} • ι_x((dβ)(t•x)) = ((q+1)·t^q) • β(t•x) + t^{q+1} • Dβ(t•x)[x].
Here ι_yα := α.curryLeft y, i.e. (ι_yα)(v_1, …, v_q) = α(y, v_1, …, v_q); d is the exterior derivative (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv); and Dβ(t•x) = fderiv ℝ β (t•x). The right side is the t-derivative of t^{q+1} • β(t•x). This is identity (∗) of the radial homotopy formula.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1)) (t : ℝ) (x : Euclid P), DifferentiableAt ℝ β (t • x) → exteriorDerivative (fun y : Euclid P => t ^ q • (β (t • y)).curryLeft y) x + t ^ (q + 1) • (exteriorDerivative β (t • x)).curryLeft x = (((q : ℝ) + 1) * t ^ q) • β (t • x) + t ^ (q + 1) • fderiv ℝ β (t • x) x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the supplied proof of radial_homotopy, stated at a single pair (t, x) and assuming only that β is differentiable at t•x.

Notation.
- Λ^j := Covector (Euclid P) j.
- ι_yα := α.curryLeft y, so (ι_yα)(v_1, …, v_j) = α(y, v_1, …, v_j). ι_y is linear in α (curryLeft_smul).
- alt := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin, a linear map L(ℝ^P, Λ^j) → Λ^{j+1}, and D := fderiv ℝ. For every ω : ℝ^P → Λ^j and every y, dω(y) = exteriorDerivative ω y = alt(Dω(y)) by definition.
- Fix t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^P. Put β_t(y) := β(t•y) and ψ_t(y) := ι_y(β_t(y)) = (β(t•y)).curryLeft y.

1. β_t is differentiable at x. The map y ↦ t•y is continuous linear, differentiable everywhere, and sends x to t•x. β is differentiable at t•x by hypothesis. Apply the chain rule.
2. Dilation chain rule: Dβ_t(x) = t • Dβ(t•x) (Mathlib fderiv_comp_smul). Directly, D(β ∘ (t·id))(x) = Dβ(t•x) ∘L (t·id) = t • Dβ(t•x); for t = 0 both sides vanish because β_0 is constant. Consequently:
 (a) dβ_t(x) = alt(t • Dβ(t•x)) = t • alt(Dβ(t•x)) = t • (dβ)(t•x), since alt is linear (alternatizeUncurryFin_smul);
 (b) Dβ_t(x)[x] = t • Dβ(t•x)[x], by evaluating the identity of continuous linear maps at x.
3. Cartan's formula for β_t. By step 1, the sibling euler_cartan (the accepted dtc_cone_euler_cartan) applies with m := q, the form β_t and the point y := x:
 dψ_t(x) + ι_x(dβ_t(x)) = ((q : ℝ) + 1) • β_t(x) + Dβ_t(x)[x].
 Substitute 2(a), 2(b), β_t(x) = β(t•x) and ι_x(t • α) = t • ι_x(α) (curryLeft_smul, then evaluation at x):
 dψ_t(x) + t • ι_x((dβ)(t•x)) = ((q : ℝ) + 1) • β(t•x) + t • Dβ(t•x)[x].   (C)
4. Constant factor. The form y ↦ t^q • ψ_t(y) is the constant multiple t^q • ψ_t. For a constant c ∈ ℝ, d(c • ω) = c • dω with no hypothesis on ω, because D(c•ω)(x) = c • Dω(x) and alt is linear (extDeriv_fun_smul; SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_smul). Hence d(y ↦ t^q • ψ_t(y))(x) = t^q • dψ_t(x).
5. Algebra. By (C), dψ_t(x) = ((q : ℝ) + 1) • β(t•x) + t • Dβ(t•x)[x] − t • ι_x((dβ)(t•x)). By step 4 and t^q·t = t^{q+1}:
 d(y ↦ t^q • ψ_t(y))(x) + t^{q+1} • ι_x((dβ)(t•x))
  = t^q • (((q : ℝ) + 1) • β(t•x)) + (t^q·t) • Dβ(t•x)[x] − (t^q·t) • ι_x((dβ)(t•x)) + t^{q+1} • ι_x((dβ)(t•x))
  = (((q : ℝ) + 1)·t^q) • β(t•x) + t^{q+1} • Dβ(t•x)[x].
 This is the claim. Every step holds for all t, including t = 0, and for q = 0 (t^0 = 1). ∎

Remark (not used in the proof). The right side is the derivative at t of s ↦ s^{q+1} • β(s•x), by the product and chain rules. The parent integrates this derivative over [0, 1].

Implementation note (verified in Lean during decomposition, about 20 lines, standard axioms only; not part of the proof):
- Step 1: hβt : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun y : Euclid P => β (t • y)) x := hβ.comp x (differentiableAt_id.const_smul t).
- Step 3: hC := Submission.dtc_cone_euler_cartan P q (fun y => β (t • y)) x hβt.
- Step 2(a): show ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ (fun y => β (t • y)) x) = t • ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ β (t • x)), then rw [fderiv_comp_smul, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul].
- Step 2(b): rw [fderiv_comp_smul]; rfl.
- Step 4: extDeriv_fun_smul (t ^ q) (fun z : Euclid P => ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft (β (t • z)) z).
- Step 5: rw [hd, hD, ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_smul, smul_apply] at hC; rw [hs, eq_sub_of_add_eq hC]; module.
proof_key_steps: β_t := β(t·) is differentiable at x. By the dilation chain rule (fderiv_comp_smul), Dβ_t(x) = t • Dβ(t•x), so dβ_t(x) = t • (dβ)(t•x) and Dβ_t(x)[x] = t • Dβ(t•x)[x].
Cartan's formula (sibling euler_cartan) for β_t at x, rewritten with these identities and curryLeft_smul: dψ_t(x) + t • ι_x((dβ)(t•x)) = (q+1) • β(t•x) + t • Dβ(t•x)[x], where ψ_t(y) = ι_y β(t•y).
d commutes with the constant factor t^q: d(y ↦ t^q • ψ_t(y))(x) = t^q • dψ_t(x).
Multiplying by t^q and using t^q·t = t^{q+1} gives d(y ↦ t^q ι_y β(t•y))(x) + t^{q+1} • ι_x((dβ)(t•x)) = ((q+1)t^q) • β(t•x) + t^{q+1} • Dβ(t•x)[x].
